site: Land at the rear of 32 Gleneldon Road / Ashlake Road, Streatham, SW16 2BD

controlledIdentity.proposal: Demolition of three existing garages and erection of a new one-bedroom dwelling.

acquisitionAttempts.route: Lambeth weekly-list publication plus Lambeth Public Access document route
observed: Lambeth's official weekly list identifies Land at the Rear of 32 Gleneldon Road, Streatham, London SW16 2BD, application 24/00124/FUL, for demolition of three garages and erection of one dwelling.
Lambeth states that its planning database contains applications from 1986 onward and that newer applications normally expose plans and documents through Public Access.
The exact application record is form-driven and the decisive source drawing/document bytes were not transported into the controlled evidence packet through the available no-spend interfaces.
acquisitionAttempts.authorityBoundary: Official weekly-list identity proves application/site/proposal identity but not parcel shape, dimensions, orientation or datum. Portal capability does not substitute for the exact source bytes.

acquisitionAttempts.route: Lambeth Public Access / Planning Data title-boundary route / address identity
observed: The planning application describes a distinct rear-garage development site, but no controlled application red-line geometry was recovered into this packet.
The host address contains multiple property interests; postcode/address records do not establish that any host title polygon equals the rear development parcel.
No exact HM Land Registry title-index entity has been identity-bound to the one-house rear parcel in this packet.
acquisitionAttempts.authorityBoundary: Host-property, postcode and marketing geometry are not substitutes for the application parcel. Any later HMLR title-index polygon remains indicative and is not a determined legal boundary.

acquisitionAttempts.route: Environment Agency LiDAR Composite DTM 1 m / postcode source-routing context
observed: Postcode-level elevation values exist publicly but vary by aggregator and are not parcel terrain evidence.
DPL accepts EA 1 m DTM as SCREENING terrain authority only when bound to a controlled site extent or frame.
Because no controlled RP-008 parcel geometry/frame has entered the evidence graph, no authoritative parcel terrain sample or ODN datum is admitted.
acquisitionAttempts.authorityBoundary: Postcode elevation is source-routing context only; it is not R4 evidence and EA DTM is not a private measured topographic survey.

acquisitionAttempts.route: Official Lambeth Ashlake Road street context plus exact-site application/marketing context
observed: Official Lambeth public material describes Ashlake Road as a two-way predominantly residential through road.
The exact-site public record and current marketing consistently place the development site behind 32 Gleneldon Road with an Ashlake Road relationship.
No controlled parcel frontage segment, entrance geometry or access relationship tied to an authoritative site extent has been recovered.
acquisitionAttempts.authorityBoundary: Street character and marketing frontage context do not prove Reference House access geometry, legal access rights or a controlled frontage segment.

acquisitionAttempts.route: Official one-dwelling application identity plus current market context
observed: The official application proves that the planning subject was a single dwelling on the rear-garage site, making the one-house experiment coherent at site-identity level.

Current marketing asserts approximately 97 square metres and depicts a consented one-house scheme, but those measurements and applicant-house geometry remain non-authoritative for Reference House fit/no-fit.
No planning-likelihood or compatibility inference is taken from the applicant scheme.
acquisitionAttempts.authorityBoundary: A previous one-house proposal establishes experiment coherence only. It does not provide controlled Reference House placement geometry.

readiness.reason: Exact application/site identity is controlled, but no placement-ready application/title geometry for the rear development parcel entered the evidence graph.
No controlled parcel shape/dimensions can honestly test the unchanged 12.0 m x 10.8 m Reference House footprint; marketing area and applicant-house geometry are explicitly non-transferable.
Street/address context is known, but no controlled application/title geometry or source drawing bytes establish the real parcel orientation frame.
No authoritative parcel terrain sample or usable ODN datum is bound to a controlled RP-008 site extent.
Ashlake Road context and the site's broad street relationship are known, but exact placement-level frontage/access geometry tied to the controlled parcel is absent.
Official application reference, site description and one-house proposal coherently identify the same rear-garage development subject.

programmeDisposition.reason: RP-004, RP-006, RP-007 and now the deliberately lower-pathology RP-008 have each failed to admit enough controlled spatial/datum evidence for candidate authoring through bounded no-spend public routes. Further convenience-selected site searching would optimize for retrievability rather than deployability and repeat the same evidence class.
